Moss01.description: Moss stripped from a rock by the armful, damp and springy. Packed into the gaps of a wattle or log wall it stops the draught -- the chinking of northern houses for thousands of years -- and it makes a soft bed.

FieldStone01.shortDescription: A heavy field stone, good for walling.
FieldStone01.description: A stone the size of a loaf, about twelve kilograms, knocked off a boulder or picked from a field: what dry walls, cobble footings and stone walls are laid from. One at a time is all anyone carries far.
